messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Details about FIRMA scores tag and time to run FIRMA
parts:
Hi Ken,

I have a detail question about the two functions
getFirmaScores.FirmaModel() and fromFiles.FirmaSet(). It seems like
getFirmaScores looks for the pattern/tag to be ",FIRMAscores" while
fromFiles seems to look for ",FIRMAresults". Shouldn't these be the
same? Then, when I run my code, I get the ",FIRMAresults" ending on the
output files, but the fit function seems to be calling getFirmaScores(),
so why are my files not ",FIRMAscores"?

Also, when I'm running the fit function it is taking a REALLY long time
(my weights/residuals have already been calculated) -- far longer than
fitting the model did. In fact at first it ran out of memory and
stopped, then I cleared all the objects from R and started again (hoping
that it will seamlessly pick up where it stopped). I think it first ran
for 1+ hours then the second start has been similar and hasn't finished
yet. Fitting the model was only 25 minutes. Is this normal? It doesn't
seem like such a complicated task comparatively.

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Details about FIRMA scores tag and time to run FIRMA
parts:
Hi,

I have a followup question that is related to the length of time of
calculating FIRMA scores. I notice that, like calculateResiduals(), the
fit.FirmaModel seems to be fitting/updating per cel file rather than
chunks of units like the PLM fit (and I have had similar problems
calculating the residuals in terms of running out of memory, etc.). What
is the logic in updating per .cel file? It seems like you can't take
account of the memory limits and have to pull in at least 2
vectors/lists of length equal to all the number of probes per iteration.
I'm also asking because I have a calculateResidual function to make for
myself, and though I'd like to just copy the existing code (and can do
it in 1 line), I'm wondering if I should actually adapt the
fit.ProbeLevelModel function so that I will avoid the memory problems.

The memory problem with the firma scores has gotten very frustrating, as
my R crashed on my second attempt at the FIRMA scores, after at least a
couple of hours (it often crashes rather than gives an error when I run
out of memory) and I don't think I'm making any progress even. Unlike
the fit for the PLM, there's not really an idea from the output where
you are, since 'units' is always all the units (since it's fit by
dataset and not by unit) and it doesn't printout the current file.
Moreover, the fit.FirmaModel function seems to use the same code to find
remaining units to fit as fit.ProbeLevelModel (which fits by unit
chunks), even though the Firma version is fitting by array. i.e. it uses
findUnitsTodo and so forth to identify the units to do. However
findUnitsTodo.FirmaSet will look at the last file of the set, and then
return units that have all zero pixel values for that file. Which means,
I think, that it will refit ALL units in ALL the files every time
because none of the units in the last file have been fitted. So it's
starting over from scratch everytime I've been running it? I notice that
calculateResiduals actually tests per array whether to fit the array, so
at least it makes progress if it crashes, though I've had problems
picking back up with calculateResiduals too. Perhaps I will make my own
version of the firma scores that will let me chose which array to fit,
rather than which units, and just do them individually and see if it
will finish.

Sorry, I know I brought up a lot of different things here.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 0e065001d5e74ca3
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Details about FIRMA scores tag and time  to run FIRMA
parts: Hi Elizabeth,

> I have a followup question that is related to the length of time of
> calculating FIRMA scores.

Firstly, to address the timing issue, I think this is tied to the fact that
with the fitting, we're fitting the model to (e.g. for the core CDF) 22010
units, while with calculating FIRMA scores, we're calling quantile() 233000 x
nbrOfArrays times (once for each group in each unit of each array).
quantile() isn't particularly fast so I think this is the culprit. I'll try
to think of ways of speeding this up a bit.

> I notice that, like calculateResiduals(), the
> fit.FirmaModel seems to be fitting/updating per cel file rather than
> chunks of units like the PLM fit (and I have had similar problems
> calculating the residuals in terms of running out of memory, etc.). What
> is the logic in updating per .cel file?

It should be faster than doing the calculations in chunks of units, because we
are storing the full chip in memory and thus saving considerably on I/O (which
is generally the biggest bottleneck in aroma.affymetrix). However, I'm
running on a Linux box with 16 GB RAM, and I can certainly understand that
most users will have less to play with than that. FYI, I was monitoring
memory usage and I don't think it ever went above 1.5 GB during the FIRMA
calculations, but behaviour on Windows might be different (and I'm not sure
how much RAM you have).

DEVEL NOTE:
-~-~-~-~-~-
Perhaps we should have an argument to methods like calculateResiduals() which
allows users to go by chunks in order to save memory.

> out of memory) and I don't think I'm making any progress even. Unlike
> the fit for the PLM, there's not really an idea from the output where
> you are, since 'units' is always all the units (since it's fit by
> dataset and not by unit) and it doesn't printout the current file.
I'll add printing of the current status.

> Moreover, the fit.FirmaModel function seems to use the same code to find
> remaining units to fit as fit.ProbeLevelModel (which fits by unit
> chunks), even though the Firma version is fitting by array. i.e. it uses
> findUnitsTodo and so forth to identify the units to do.

This is a design flaw. If we're going array-by-array then findUnitsTodo
should be checking per array. I will fix this.

Cheers,

Ken

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Details about FIRMA scores tag and time to run FIRMA
parts:
Hi,

a comment about memory usage of calculateResiduals(). This method is
implement such that it calculated the residuals array by array.
Basically what is stored in memory at any time is the probe
affinities, the chip effects (expanded to each probe), and the probe
intensities, plus some index vectors to optimize reading/writing.
Roughly we use 3 doubles and 3 integers per cell, that is 3*8+3*4=36
bytes per cell. With 6553600 cells that is 225 MB per array. It does
not make much sense to optimize this further by calculating the
residuals in chunks of units.

I just tested on my WinXP with 19 Mapping250K_Nsp chips;

> cdf
AffymetrixCdfFile:
Path: annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Nsp
Filename: Mapping250K_Nsp.cdf
Filesize: 185.45MB
Chip type: Mapping250K_Nsp
Dimension: 2560x2560
Number of cells: 6553600
Number of units: 262338
Cells per unit: 24.98
Number of QC units: 6

and the memory usage never goes above 750MB. I looked at the code and
it is possible to optimize the memory usage even further (which will
be available in the next update). I especially noticed that the first
time you calling calculateResiduals() on a new chip type you will use
more memory compared to subsequent calls on the same chip type. When
I restarted R and reran it, the second time the memory usage was never
above 350MB, which is very much in line with the above estimates of
225 MB / array + package overheads etc.

DETAILS: The reason is that the first time it queries the CDF and
restructures lists etc without garbage collecting as often as
possible, which makes the memory image grow. The second time, these
results are loaded from cache files and there is no memory allocation
for restructuring lists. Note: When running R in Windows, when you
allocate memory for a large object and then remove it, the garbage
collection will clean it out from the R memory, but unfortunately
Windows will not get this memory back until R exits. It might be that
your exon CDF structure needs even more memory, but it should never
crash.

SUGGESTION 1: Get Process Explorer
(http://www.microsoft.com/technet/sysinternals/utilities/ProcessExplorer.mspx)
to follow the memory usage in more details. For instance, you can
quite easy identify peaks correlating with loading of data etc. Try
to identify where and when your memory is getting "wasted/lost".

SUGGESTION 2: Make use of the 'verbose' argument, which for many
methods give details on what is going on and now more often also
output the result after each garbage collection, which gives you more
details on the amount of memory allocated for object in R. The more
negative value you use, the more details, e.g. verbose=-5 (I use
this).

Cheers

Henrik

Hi Ken,

My computer is 2GB of RAM, but its dual processor, so I think that means
I effectively have 1GB for running firma, so that sounds like from your
FIRMA run that it wouldn't be enough even if I weren't running in Windows.

I did eventually run it array by array (just adjusting the code and then
putting a for loop on the outside of the call to fit -- basically taking
the place of the for loop within the fit). I ran out of memory after the
21st array and so I restarted it there and finished the last. It was
about 6 minutes per array so it took a very long time, though clearly
that is repeating a lot of expensive operations (it said about 88% time
spent on the fitting in the output). The gc() results printed out for
the last of the 2nd batch (the 14th array in that cycle) was

used (Mb) gc trigger (Mb) max used (Mb)
Ncells 21242259 567.3 34190145 913.0 34190145 913.0
Vcells 32953627 251.5 51301351 391.4 51285183 391.3

Victoria also said that the firma calculations were very slow, though
they finished for her--she is running off a statistics department server.

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 0e065001d5e74ca3
messages.subject: FIRMA optimisation (was Re: Details about FIRMA scores tag and  time to run FIRMA)
parts: Hi Elizabeth,

> I did eventually run it array by array (just adjusting the code and then
> putting a for loop on the outside of the call to fit -- basically taking
> the place of the for loop within the fit).

FYI, I've now modified the code so that it checks array-by-array whether units
have been fitted. This should be in the next update.

> I ran out of memory after the
> 21st array and so I restarted it there and finished the last. It was
> about 6 minutes per array so it took a very long time

That tallies with my experience (6-8 minutes per array). I'm pretty sure that
the bottleneck is the use of quantile() and the fact we're having to call it
for > 2e5 units. Haven't thought of a speed-up yet. Sorry for my inefficient
code - goal #1 was to get a working version ready quickly, and I haven't
gotten round to optimisation yet... I'll try to find a solution quickly but
can't promise anything as next week is my last week at WEHI and any future
work on aroma.affymetrix is going to be a spare time activity.

Cheers,

Ken
